rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 4-5 (Figures 4-1, 5-1 to 5-7): the authors report their own Proteus simulation runs of a Raspberry Pi/MCP3208 IoT framework with temperature, pressure, soil moisture and rain sensors over a 1-hour simulated period, plus a ThingSpeak/mobile-app integration producing alerts and a moving-average forecast.
rows.notes: Q2 no: the study is a Proteus circuit simulation driven by predefined input data (Section 5.1, 5.5); it is never compared with measurements from a real field or real hardware (Section 6 states explicitly it was not conducted with real-world devices). It reports no crop yield, resource-use or environmental-impact outcome, only simulated sensor readings, LCD/cloud display and threshold alerts. Yield improvement and reduced water waste are asserted in the discussion with citations to other work, not measured. The study at most demonstrates the monitoring/alerting function that is a precondition of the claimed precise-management-to-yield effect, hence upstream = true. The authors do state limitations (predefined data, no calibration, no real devices, basic forecasting) but these concern the simulation, not any result on the claimed yield effect, so Q8 remains no under rule 3.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references). Figures are not reproduced. The paper is a system-design/simulation paper with no field deployment, no crop data and no validation against observations.
